anti_generic_signature_read: The specific spire, arched crown, wedge tower and rooftop tanks make a coherent Manhattan chess skyline rather than an assortment of unrelated miniatures. Common stepped plinths and recessed facades unify all roles. The urban perimeter is physical relief rather than applied neighborhood names.
blind_action_read: The paired board views show a starting arrangement and both pawn rows advanced toward the middle while major pieces remain behind. This visually communicates movable chess pieces and an evolving chess position, without demonstrating a legal single-move transition or tested physical play.
blind_form_read: Upright volumetric architectural bodies with visible side faces, stepped octagonal bases, setbacks, facade grooves and distinctive crowns; a shallow square board with integrated perimeter relief. The forms look substantial and individually separated on their squares.
blind_held_read: An unmistakable physical chess set: a shallow checkerboard with two opposing cream and dark teal armies, six piece families and freestanding chessmen. Blind observations were persisted in round3-blind.json before Wish or concept reveal.
blind_relationship_read: Both armies use the same skyline vocabulary and face each other across a continuous checkerboard. Taller landmarks occupy back-rank roles, repeated water tanks occupy pawn roles, and a common low border links the urban reliefs around the playing field.
blind_subjects_read: Chess was immediately recognizable. The stepped spire evoked Empire State, the tiered arched crown evoked Chrysler, the wedge tower evoked Flatiron, and the pawns evoked rooftop water tanks. Horse knights and crenellated rooks were clear. Border close-ups showed facades, a vehicle-like profile, arches, paired spiral ornaments and a columned structure; exact community identities were uncertain before reveal.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: The clean cream/teal palette, shared octagonal stepped plinths, controlled facade language and recognizable skyline families produce a visually cohesive finished set. Desirability is this reviewer's visual judgment, not evidence of customer response or legal novelty.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: A beautiful, coherent, original-looking collectible New York chess set.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Six different silhouettes and a descending height hierarchy distinguish the families; horse and rook forms are conventional, landmark royal forms are distinct, the wedge is distinct from both, and tank pawns are shortest. Cream versus dark teal clearly distinguishes sides. The role key remains useful for first use.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Clearly distinguish six chess roles and opposing sides.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: The two views retain the standard board, opening rank organization and separate piece footprints; the changed view shows freely repositioned pawns. Full legal-rule compliance is outside a still-image review.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Broad flat plinths, substantial lower bodies, blunt crowns and separately spaced pieces visibly support this form requirement. Supplied preflight is bound by its hash, but rendered appearance and digital preflight do not establish actual printing, stability, comfort, fit or durability.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Provide stable-looking, graspable chessmen and practical printable form.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: The visible object consists of a board, inlays and passive free-standing chess pieces, with no electronic device, wiring, switch or powered function shown.

largest_risk: Exact community recognition is the weakest visual layer. Before reveal I did not identify the five neighborhoods from their small reliefs; paired turntables and elevated transit initially read as ornaments and a columned facade. The researched illustrated identification key is necessary to teach the intended Chinatown, Williamsburg, Bronx, Staten Island and Queens connections. Dark-side facade detail is subdued in the overview.
